title: OpenAI ChatCompletions provenance + instrumentation mapping layer
creator: Marina Cortez
description:
Problem: When proxying or translating OpenAI Chat Completions traffic into Redwood's internal request/response model we lose useful provenance and instrumentation signals (which agent injected system messages, client-supplied trace IDs, token-level timing, tool invocation lineage). This causes gaps in Console tracing, makes debugging customer incidents hard, and prevents precise billing/attribution in hybrid flows.

Goal: Implement a compatibility mapping layer that preserves and surfaces provenance and instrumentation metadata end-to-end while remaining compatible with clients expecting vanilla OpenAI CC shapes. The mapping must work for both HTTP and streaming (SSE/HTTP2) flows and must not expose sensitive customer data to Redwood telemetry in plaintext unless customer allows it via config.

Scope: request/response mapping for Chat Completions (messages + function_call), streaming event envelopes (token frames), and tool/function calling artifacts. Backwards-compatibility for existing clients is required; support will be gated behind a feature flag per-customer and can be disabled for strict OA-compat profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Provenance tags (agent: system|assistant|tool|client) are attached to every message we surface in Console and included in structured output when the customer enables provenance passthrough
Streaming token frames include an explicit minimal envelope field 'rdwd_prov' when feature flag is on; existing SSE consumer behavior remains unchanged if flag is off
Function/tool invocations are annotated with an invocation_id and caller_provenance and that metadata is preserved in retries and in fallback model handoffs
No more than 5% P50 latency regression on typical 2-8 token responses in canary compared to baseline
Automated integration tests covering HTTP chat, HTTP streaming, and function call flows pass in CI (coverage for edge cases: partial tool outputs, multi-tool seq, tool-offline fallback)
Design doc + data-retention privacy knobs reviewed and approved by Security before beta rollout
steps: Draft design doc that defines the envelope format, header conventions, and privacy redaction rules (Marina)
Implement mapping middleware that attaches provenance header X-RDWD-Provenance and optional X-RDWD-Trace for legacy OA-compat paths (Daniel)
Extend streaming server to emit rdwd_prov envelope on token frames when flag enabled; ensure SSE framing & chunk boundaries preserved (Eng)
Add invocation_id generation and persistence for function/tool calls; thread invocation_id through retries and fallback route selection (Eng)
Add unit + integration tests; create synthetic harness for high-concurrency streaming to measure latency impact (QA)
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for customers who opt-in via console (SRE + Product)
Collect metrics and perform incident/bug triage; if telemetry shows >5% regression, revert and iterate (SRE)
Prepare docs for Public API/Console showing new provenance opt-in and how to interpret fields (Docs + DevRel)
comments: 2025-02-10 Marina Cortez: Created ticket. Attached initial problem statement and examples of lost provenance (system injection lost when normalizing OA messages).
2025-02-12 Daniel Kim: Pulled into planned cycle. I'll prototype header-based approach and a streaming envelope extension; will validate with the streaming hub.
2025-02-17 PM review (Sofia Nguyen): Need clear privacy defaults: provenance OFF by default; customers can enable explicit passthrough. Also add retention TTL settings for traced token timings.
2025-02-20 Security (Owen Li): Flagged detection of 'client-supplied-trace' header — must be sanitized and only accepted if customer-managed KMS allows. Security review required before rollouts.

2025-02-24 Engineering spike: Prototype shows ~2.8% P50 regression on microbench workload with rdwd_prov present. Token-level timing serialization added 80B avg per token frame — acceptable but needs careful batching to avoid amplification.
2025-03-01 UX (Priya Ramesh): Console UI mockups uploaded to design doc; will need to show provenance timeline in the token inspector and a filter for 'tool vs assistant vs system' messages.
2025-03-03 Daniel Kim: Implementation branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/ENG-631044-provenance-mapper. Draft PR when tests green.
